description: Chain-link diamond-mesh fence panel stretched between two galvanised steel pipe posts with a top rail and tension wire.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Chain-link fence panel of galvanised diamond wire mesh stretched between two round steel pipe posts with a horizontal top rail, a bottom tension wire, and a small concrete footing at the base of each post Materials: Galvanised wire dulled grey with rust at the ties, posts rust-streaked, mesh sagging slightly and bent at the bottom edge, dry weeds at the footings.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.91. ~1,800/4,000 triangles, 3/4 draw calls, 3/3 materials, 3/6 unique geometries, three canvases at 0.7 MB, factory ~60 ms. Turntable: the mesh is open by nature, allowed on measurement; 90/270 are UNSEGMENTABLE by size (post and footing under 2% of frame against the segmenter's 3.5% floor), recorded as a gate limitation of every 3 m panel.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope built at 3.18 x 2.04 x 0.36 m (one post per tile; rail and wire overrun 0.13 m into the next tile's post); post r 0.048 (the plate's pipe is 28 px of a 560 px fence = 0.10 m), rail at 1.94 m, footing 0.36 m and the draped mesh 0.24-1.90 m off the proxy's 0.98 / 0.10 / 0.14-0.92 H. Band table: mean |delta width| 0.035, |delta depth| 0.023.
featureReviews.notes: The first build's r 0.03 post and r 0.02 rail were half the plate's pipe.

featureReviews.evidence: Alpha-cut diamond lattice at an 85 mm cell on a 24 x 6 pane that HANGS: its top edge droops 0.055 in each of the five tie-to-tie spans between the hog rings on the rail (per-span drape, `sagSpans`) and its bottom follows the tension wire's 0.09 sag (fence template gained pane `segs` / `sagTop` / `sagBot`). Wire tone 205 at metalness 0.05 reads bright galvanised at 0, 180 and 315 degrees where the first build's 0.30-metal lattice rendered dark.
featureReviews.notes: The wire thins with distance as the alpha mips average out; the knuckles are dots, not twists.

featureReviews.evidence: Heavy pipe with a two-part domed cap, four tension bands, a rail cup and four ties, rust canvas at density 80; a two-step concrete footing 0.36 x 0.28 in 44 dry weed blades on the concrete material's vertex colours.
featureReviews.notes: Weeds are blades, not tufts with seed heads.

name: Chain-Link Fence Panel
nameTh: รั้วลวดตาข่าย
notes: Lot boundaries, school yards, substation compounds. The mesh is an alpha-cut texture on a single plane, not modelled wire -- a prop kit for low-end PCs cannot afford geometry mesh. Tiles post to post. Placement overridden to floor. Not breakable. One post per tile: the post is on the -X end and the bay runs to the +X edge, so tiles chain along X with no doubled post at a joint.
